selectedClaim.subject: fermentation-room wall display
selectedClaim.property: temperature reading at 06:40

cases.sourceRationale: The selected claim is an observed temperature reading. Equivalent descriptors may name the room's displayed temperature; retain the reading and time. The source establishes no setpoint choice.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Treating a displayed number as a chosen temperature, or dropping the real temperature descriptors to produce unknown.

selectedClaim.subject: sealed crates in the loading bay
selectedClaim.property: count on Monday morning

cases.sourceRationale: Counting establishes the crate count at the stated time, not a chosen shipment quantity. The counter can appear in attribution, but the selected proposition must remain the count.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Converting an inventory count to an adopted packing plan or discarding the count as unsupported.

selectedClaim.subject: test dough
selectedClaim.property: rise during its first hour in the bowl

cases.sourceRationale: This is a negative observation of dough behavior. Both the absence of rising and the one-hour limit are part of the target meaning.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Reading did not rise as rejection of rising, or losing the negation when selecting the claim.

selectedClaim.subject: faint click during the suitcase test
selectedClaim.property: possible origin
selectedClaim.value: may have come from the latch

cases.sourceRationale: The source tentatively attributes an observed click to the latch. The possible origin is useful supported meaning even though its causal certainty is limited.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Making the latch a confirmed cause or a considered design choice, or erasing the tentative origin.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: feeling after the language exam on 2026-02-17

cases.sourceRationale: The source reports a dated feeling after an exam, with no chosen stance or settled preference. An equivalent tuple can place the date in scope or applies.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Calling relief an adopted choice or enduring personality trait, or dropping the feeling to obtain unknown.

selectedClaim.subject: parcel
selectedClaim.property: weight at dispatch as reported by Lale

cases.sourceRationale: Lale reports a parcel weight. The reporter relationship and dispatch time may live in other qualification fields, but the target remains the weight observation.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Inferring that either Lale or the user chose a 740-gram target weight, or replacing parcel weight with a generic report event.

selectedClaim.subject: scanner lamp
selectedClaim.property: flickering during the morning scan

cases.sourceRationale: The card selects lamp behavior. The external-drive backup choice is a separate source clause. A baseline tuple selecting backup storage instead is wrong-selected-claim and is not an observation commitment result.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Borrowing adopted from the drive choice, or switching the selected tuple to drive storage to manufacture a commitment result.

selectedClaim.subject: trial loaf
selectedClaim.property: center texture when cut at noon

cases.sourceRationale: Sticky texture is an observation, while the lower rack is a separately chosen action for the next batch. A tuple about rack selection is wrong-selected-claim even though its commitment could be adopted.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Applying the next-batch rack decision to the observed sticky center or replacing texture with rack choice.

selectedClaim.subject: Platform 3
selectedClaim.property: crowding at the user's 08:15 arrival

cases.sourceRationale: The card describes platform crowding. Selecting a return-trip seat in the quiet carriage is a distinct adopted action. Judge the target match before commitment; selecting the carriage instead is wrong-selected-claim.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Treating the crowding as adopted because the source also contains a seat choice, or changing the tuple to that choice.

selectedClaim.subject: delivery carton
selectedClaim.property: corner condition on arrival

cases.sourceRationale: The arrival condition is the selected observation. Settling on foam sleeves concerns next week's shipment. Selecting sleeves is wrong-selected-claim, not a valid alternative target for this card.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Transferring the packaging decision to the dented corner or suppressing the observed damage.

selectedClaim.subject: cart's front wheel
selectedClaim.property: behavior during the user's checkout test

cases.sourceRationale: The card selects the user's wheel observation. Odo's quoted rubber-wheel choice is separate and belongs to Odo. A baseline tuple selecting wheel material is wrong-selected-claim, regardless of its commitment.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Borrowing Odo's adoption for the wobble, treating Odo's choice as the user's, or replacing wobble with material selection.

selectedClaim.subject: rehearsal recording's opening passage
selectedClaim.property: audible echo

cases.sourceRationale: The target is the absence of audible echo in a recording. The microphone choice concerns Saturday's performance. A tuple about microphone selection is wrong-selected-claim and cannot score as this target.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Converting no echo into a rejection, assigning the microphone decision to acoustic behavior, or losing the negation.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: thermostat setpoint choice for the fermentation room's overnight cycle

cases.sourceRationale: The source explicitly chooses the 18°C setpoint. Equivalent tuples may use the thermostat as subject if they retain the chosen setpoint rather than inventing an observed reading. First match the actual baseline tuple semantically, then assess commitment using its polarity; labels need not match literally.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: forgoing the chosen setpoint for the fermentation room's overnight cycle

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: Accept only a negative encoding of the same explicit 18°C choice within the same cycle, not an invented discussion or rejection of a particular alternative temperature.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Downgrading a stated choice to unknown merely because its value is numeric or its kind is fact, or replacing a setpoint with a measurement.

selectedClaim.subject: Pavel
selectedClaim.property: table choice for his workshop's lunch area

cases.sourceRationale: Pavel's quoted words explicitly establish his choice. The quote is sufficient for Pavel's represented commitment, with quoted attribution; it does not establish reporter adoption. Match the actual baseline tuple semantically before assessing commitment according to its polarity.

selectedClaim.subject: Pavel
selectedClaim.property: forgoing his chosen table for his workshop's lunch area

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: Accept only if the tuple means the same bounded round-table choice by Pavel. Do not invent rejection of a particular other shape or transfer ownership to the reporter.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Assigning Pavel's choice to the user or calling the represented choice unknown simply because it was quoted.

selectedClaim.subject: volunteer team
selectedClaim.property: badge choice for the chess tournament

cases.sourceRationale: The assistant conveys the team's explicit settled choice. Reported attribution preserves this relationship; speaker role does not negate the represented team's commitment. Judge a semantically matching baseline tuple's actual polarity rather than requiring the canonical wording.

selectedClaim.subject: volunteer team
selectedClaim.property: forgoing its chosen badges for the chess tournament

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: Accept only a negative encoding of the same settled reusable-badge choice for this tournament, without inventing any particular rejected replacement or reporter adoption.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Treating the report as an assistant suggestion, moving ownership to the user, or erasing the team's explicit adoption.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: added-ice choice for all three tasting-flight drinks

cases.sourceRationale: The user explicitly decides to serve the drinks without added ice. Adopted no-ice service and rejected ice addition can encode the same bounded decision. Match the actual baseline tuple semantically first, then judge commitment against that tuple's polarity; do not use automatic word matching.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: ice-addition option for all three tasting-flight drinks

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: The tuple must refer to adding ice to these three drinks and preserve the explicit serving decision, not a general dislike of ice or an observation that ice was absent.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Calling this explicit serving decision unknown, rejecting the no-ice option itself, or adopting the ice-addition option itself. An equivalent rejected ice-addition tuple is valid.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: lining option for the instrument case

cases.sourceRationale: The user explicitly considers cork and states that the lining is not settled. Both the option and its tentative status must survive semantic paraphrase.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Treating a named option as adopted, treating lack of a settled choice as rejection, or deleting the option.

selectedClaim.subject: Nela
selectedClaim.property: start-time option for her cycling trip

cases.sourceRationale: Nela's quoted message weighs sunrise while comparison remains unfinished. This represents Nela's consideration and does not transfer a choice to the user.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Assigning consideration or adoption to the reporter, or turning Nela's tentative option into a settled start time.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: collection schedule option for bakery returns

cases.sourceRationale: Not committed excludes adoption but does not mean rejection: the next sentence explicitly keeps weekly pickup under consideration.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Interpreting not committed as rejected or unknown while ignoring the explicit consideration of weekly pickup.

selectedClaim.subject: knitting club
selectedClaim.property: venue option for its winter meetup

cases.sourceRationale: The assistant reports club minutes that explicitly consider the greenhouse with a vote pending. This is the club's represented consideration, not an assistant recommendation.
cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Inferring adoption before the vote, treating the reported option as the user's preference, or assigning unknown solely due to assistant role.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: lid option for the spice jars

cases.sourceRationale: Ruled out explicitly rejects steel lids. The metallic smell explains the rejection but is not the selected lid option. Rejected steel lids and an adopted decision to avoid steel lids can express the same bounded decision; judge commitment against the actual semantically matching tuple's polarity.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: lid exclusion for the spice jars

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: Accept only the decision to avoid steel lids for these jars, without inventing a chosen replacement material or a general aversion to steel.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Selecting the smell observation instead of the lid decision, adopting steel lids themselves, or calling the explicit decision unknown.

selectedClaim.subject: Rafi
selectedClaim.property: location option for his studio desk

cases.sourceRationale: Rafi explicitly rejects the mezzanine in quoted speech. The quoted rejection belongs to Rafi, while the low ceiling supplies its reason. An adopted decision to exclude the mezzanine is equivalent; first match the baseline tuple's decision meaning, then assess commitment using its polarity.

selectedClaim.subject: Rafi
selectedClaim.property: location exclusion for his studio desk
selectedClaim.value: keep the desk off the mezzanine

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: Retain Rafi's ownership and the same desk-location exclusion. Do not imply that another location was selected or that the reporter made the choice.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Assigning the decision to the reporter, selecting only the ceiling observation, or losing the explicit exclusion of the mezzanine.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: bell-addition option for the library's book-return slot

cases.sourceRationale: Decided against explicitly rejects adding a bell. Rejected bell addition and adopted no-bell addition encode the same decision. First judge whether the actual baseline tuple preserves that decision, then assess commitment according to the tuple's polarity; a polarity change alone is not wrong-selected-claim.

selectedClaim.subject: user
selectedClaim.property: bell-addition choice for the library's book-return slot

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: Accept the settled choice not to add a bell to this slot. Do not infer that an existing bell was removed, that every library bell is opposed, or that its physical absence was observed.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Adopting bell addition itself, rejecting the decision to omit bell addition, or replacing the decision with the separate disturbance premise.

selectedClaim.subject: race organizers
selectedClaim.property: surface option for the finish lane

cases.sourceRationale: The assistant conveys an explicit ruling out of gravel by the organizers. Reported ownership is separate from the source role and from the stated accessibility reason. An adopted exclusion of gravel is equivalent; judge the actual baseline tuple semantically before assigning its polarity-appropriate commitment.

selectedClaim.subject: race organizers
selectedClaim.property: surface exclusion for the finish lane

acceptedEquivalentTargets.condition: Accept only the same organizers' settled exclusion of gravel for this lane, without asserting that a particular alternative surface was chosen.

cases.forbiddenInterpretation: Replacing the surface decision with the accessibility premise, attributing the decision to the user, adopting gravel itself, or treating the explicit decision as unknown.
